title: Nicholas Ty takes oath as new Deputy Ombudsman
summary: Lawyer Nicholas Felix Ty took his oath on Thursday, November 26, 2026, as the new deputy ombudsman for Luzon.

blocks.text: Lawyer Nicholas Felix Ty took his oath on Thursday, November 26, 2026, as the new deputy ombudsman for Luzon.

Before his appointment, he served as an undersecretary at the Department of Justice (DOJ), overseeing legal and inter-agency initiatives, including efforts to address human trafficking and transnational crimes.
Upon taking his oath, Ty expressed gratitude to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. for giving him the continued opportunity to serve in public office.
In his new role, Ty said one of his priorities is to serve as a loyal soldier to Ombudsman Jesus Crispin “Boying” Remulla to help fulfill the latter’s goal of eradicating corruption in the country.
“Ang mga priorities natin bilang Deputy Ombudsman ng Luzon ay siyempre tulungan ang kasalukuyang nakaupong Ombudsman si Ombudsman Boying Remulla,” Ty said.
(Our priorities as Deputy Ombudsman for Luzon are, of course, to assist the sitting Ombudsman, Ombudsman Boying Remulla.)
“At ako naman ay magiging isang tapat na sundalo dito kay Ombudsman Remulla upang matuloy talaga ang kaniyang hangad na masugpo ang korapsyon dito sa bansa natin,” he added.
(And for my part, to be a loyal soldier to Ombudsman Remulla so that his goal of stamping out corruption in our country can truly be achieved.)
Ty said he believes the experience and insights he gained during his stint at the DOJ will prove useful in his new position at the Office of the Ombudsman.
He vowed to remain faithful to the Constitution and his sworn duties to hold violators accountable.

“Maging tapat talaga sa Konstitusyon, maging tapat sa mga batas, maging tapat sa mga tungkulin ng isang public servant at talagang maging ehemplo sa ibang mga public servant at siyempre tulungan ang ating Ombudsman para panagutin ang mga taong lumalabag sa kanilang mga obligasyon,” the new deputy ombudsman said.

(To truly be faithful to the Constitution, faithful to the laws, faithful to the duties of a public servant, to truly serve as an example to other public servants, and of course, to help our Ombudsman hold accountable those who violate their obligations.)
Ty graduated from the University of the Philippines College of Law.
He earned his Master of Laws in International Economics and Business Law from Kyushu University in Japan.
He has practiced law for more than 20 years and has also taught as an assistant professor at the UP College of Law. —Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/LDF, GMA News
